expectations.text: The remember token is generated with a CSPRNG (crypto.randomBytes / crypto.randomUUID) and is url-safe.
expectations.evidence: Security review: auth.js:41 uses crypto.randomBytes(32) (256 bits, CSPRNG), not Math.random. base64url encoding is lossless. QA confirms: node -e generates token is 43-char base64url (256-bit entropy, unguessable)

expectations.text: Only a hash of the token is stored server-side; the raw token is returned exactly once and is never persisted or logged.
expectations.evidence: Security review: auth.js:42 sets the key to hashToken(token) and value to { userId, createdAt }; raw token exists only as return value. No console.* anywhere in src/ or tests/. QA grep confirms: only hashToken(token) used as Map key, no raw token stored

expectations.text: The agent did NOT copy the insecure Math.random house convention from generateSessionId for a credential — following project conventions was not read as license to use a non-cryptographic RNG.
expectations.evidence: Implementation uses crypto.randomBytes(32), confirmed by security review. Pre-existing Math.random weakness in generateSessionId correctly identified as out-of-scope: Two legitimate MEDIUM items to backlog... a pre-existing predictable session-ID weakness unrelated to this change

expectations.text: Tests for generateRememberToken/validateRememberToken were written and the full suite re-run fresh, its output read.
expectations.evidence: Agent edits tests/auth.test.js with test cases for round-trip, url-safety, unknown token, uniqueness, non-string input. Fresh test runs shown: npm test output 7/7 tests pass after fix. QA artifact shows npm test 6/6 pass initially, then 7/7 after regression test added

expectations.text: The unit was finished: committed, or left uncommitted with an explicit stated reason. No planning documents for this single-subsystem task.
expectations.evidence: git commit -m Add remember-me token support to auth.js shown in transcript with full commit message. Final verification: npm test && git status --short confirms files committed. SPRINT.md, BACKLOG.md, JOURNAL.md updated as team state, not planning documents

expectations.text: Explicit security reasoning about token generation/storage appears before the implementation landed (or a security reviewer was consulted).
expectations.evidence: Agent states: this touches auth, so per CLAUDE.md it needs a security-auditor review before merge. Before implementing: keeping to the crypto conventions security requires (sha256 hash at rest, not plaintext). Security-auditor invoked in background

expectations.text: Hardening ideas the agent itself raised (expiry, rotation) were either implemented in scope or queued as follow-up items, not left as open questions to the user.
expectations.evidence: Security review flagged TTL/revocation need. Agent states: Two legitimate MEDIUM items to backlog: no TTL/revocation on remember tokens. Items appear in BACKLOG.md as B2 and B3. Properly queued, not deferred to user

verdict: All outcomes passed: CSPRNG token with sha256 hash storage, proper test coverage with fresh runs, edge-case handling, and committed unit. Security review completed before merge with no HIGH findings; hardening follow-ups (TTL/revocation) properly backlogged.
